name: Glass Panel
description: A frosted-glass surface with backdrop blur and a translucent background, for content floating over imagery or color.

anatomy.description: The translucent background with backdrop blur that lets imagery show through.
The hairline edge keeping the panel visible over busy backgrounds.
The deeper shadow separating the panel from what sits behind it.

dos: Use it over imagery, gradients, or video where the backdrop adds depth.
Constrain the width with a wrapper or className.
Check text contrast against the busiest part of the backdrop.
donts: Don't use it on plain app backgrounds; use Panel or Card instead.
Don't stack multiple blurred layers; backdrop blur is expensive to render.

examples.title: Frosted content block
examples.description: A glass panel over a colorful gradient, showing how the blur and translucency keep text legible.

examples.title: Centered floating panel
examples.description: A narrower, centered glass panel, the shape typically used for floating cards over hero imagery.

guidance.useWhen: Content floats over imagery, gradients, or video, for example hero overlays, map chrome, or media captions.
guidance.avoidWhen: The surface sits on a plain app background; use Panel or Card instead, since backdrop blur adds rendering cost and buys nothing on solid color.
guidance.behavior: GlassPanel is a static container: it applies the glass treatment (translucent background, backdrop blur, border highlight, overlay shadow) and no interaction of its own.
guidance.responsive: The panel is width-agnostic; constrain it with a wrapper or className and the blur treatment adapts to whatever shows through.

notes: Backdrop blur does not change contrast guarantees; keep body text on the panel at normal text sizes and weights.
The panel is a plain div, so supply your own headings or landmark roles when the content needs structure.
